why: Both made the identical, correct migration decision (wrap the per-message client rather than repoint base_url), but A verified far more of it — 10 live runs, text and image through the real on_message, a genuine fall-through test on the fallback list — and ranked its improvements on measured cost and latency instead of quoted doc numbers, including two levers it measured and then deliberately rejected. B's one clear win is the finding A got wrong (the {date}/{time} clock sits at the head of every request and destroys the cacheable prefix, which A's identical-prefix experiment never exercised), plus the deepest structural idea in either report, but most of B's leverage is unbuilt proposals with 'loses: nothing' where real caveats exist.
A_best: Measured the dominant lever properly: gpt-5.5/high at $0.0215-0.0281 and 17-21s per reply versus gpt-6-luna/low at $0.00008-0.00027 and 3-10s, shipped it as a tested branch with the conservative effort-only alternative as an explicit either/or, and caught that llmcord's VISION_MODEL_TAGS matching requires the ':vision' suffix — then live-verified an image turn still works.
B_best: Spotted that the system prompt's clock is the first thing in every request, so llmcord's resend-the-whole-chain design can never hit the prompt cache, and fixed it with a careful line-level split that leaves clock-free prompts byte-identical; r1 (collapse the provider table and make the model a per-channel choice now that one key serves every vendor) is the sharpest system-level judgment in either report.
A_worst: Concluded from an experiment it designed itself that 'reply chains in a Discord thread already get the discount for free' — the repeated-prefix test bypassed the clock that makes real llmcord requests unique every second, so it dismissed the app's largest input-cost lever on evidence that didn't model the app; provider_timeout 180s is also slack for a path a human is watching type.
B_worst: Thin verification relative to its claims: 3 live requests total, i1's savings imported from other models' ROUTER.md measurements, the fallback branch only ever observed the primary serving (no fall-through proven), the cheap-model item left entirely unbuilt and unmeasured, and m1/i2 claim 'loses: nothing' while A documents the real caveats (extra_headers/extra_query dropped on the Router path, an extra failed round trip on refusal).
